This is the trap option recycling the earlier 'mirrored her grandmother's actions' motif, which the narrative has just reversed.

Finite temporal clause 'before she added any extra toppings' attaches grammatically to 'had already started to eat hers'. Logically it encodes the intended contrast: grandmother spreads cream and jam on her scone, whereas Chloe began eating hers plain. The 'in fact' elaboration is a proper intensification: not merely started before topping it — it was mostly all in her mouth already. No contradiction with any stated fact; sole surviving candidate.

'started to eat hers taking a sip of her sweet tea first' is a temporally incoherent participial adjunct (simultaneous participle vs. 'first' sequencing clash), and the sip-of-tea motif belongs to the earlier waiting scene. Nothing in 'mostly all in her mouth already' supports a tea-sipping manner reading.
Grammatical as a participial adjunct, but factually contradicted: 'all the sandwiches were eaten up' before the scone episode, so there is no 'another delicate sandwich' to reach for.

Grammatical as a participial adjunct, but logically incompatible with the 'in fact' clause: if the scone is 'mostly all in her mouth already', there is no meaningful 'rest' to offer; moreover the grandmother has her own scone she is actively preparing. The elaboration would refute rather than intensify the blank.
